body: doc-handoff-commit-rewrite-reading: Evidence, re-verified: reading (a) is built. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:557-568 ({{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}) rewrites the documentation sprint's Window line 'Planned against commit <sha>.' only where the HEAD printed before the first commit is the commit /plan-docs recorded and 'git diff --name-only <the tree /plan-docs recorded at its window> HEAD -- <every path the commits named>' prints nothing; otherwise it leaves the line. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/SKILL.md:26 records both the commit and the window tree (a write-tree over a private index). plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:106 reads the line (PLANNED_COMMIT), and docs start exits 2 where a commit after it bears on a planned docspec with a change the plan did not read (doc-sprint-document.md step 3). Filed facts hold. Mechanism: the handoff commits paths outside .ok-planner/ after the plan's window; without a rewrite, docs start weighs those commits against the plan and stops the run; an unconditional rewrite (the defect i42 fixed) hid product commits made after the window from the next documentation window. Corpus: silent. No concept, story, or decision under .ok-planner/design/ names the handoff, the planned commit, or docs start (grep for 'handoff', 'Planned against', 'docs start', 'planned commit' finds nothing); story:keep-documentation-current and decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window speak only to the stamp opening the window. Harm: none today; the question is which reading the product commits to, and whether to commit it in the corpus at all. Options: (A) commit reading (a) to the corpus, as built: cost, the window-tree record and the two-condition test stay as tooling every /plan-docs run carries, and the corpus grows a decision on a handoff detail. (B) commit reading (b): drop the rewrite so docs start weighs every handoff commit: cost, any commit of out-of-band work at the handoff that bears on a docspec forces the owner to plan again, and the window-tree record in plan-docs step 2 is removed. (C, missed by the filer) keep reading (a) as built and write no corpus artifact: the fixer's verified call stands as a tooling choice; cost, the choice stays unrecorded and a later fixer could change it with no commitment to check against. No stated rule decides between them; this is a product-intent ruling, recommended (A) or (C) since (a) is built and verified. Siblings: doc-sprint-fixed-check-file-has-no-style-task and doc-sprint-lists-classes-in-one-checker-task touch the same documentation sprint template but bear on other steps; rule independently.

scenario-list-decision-bundles-several-choices: Evidence, re-verified: .ok-planner/design/decisions/scenario-list-decided-once.md (1785 words) still holds every choice the filer lists, unsplit: its Choice section opens with the committed scenario list and its per-story test stamp, then 'The project owns its suite run end to end' (testing.run, one results stream per run, one append of the round under a short lock, a second whole-suite round refuses), then '/plan-sprint proposes the list for the stories a sprint takes or must re-plan' with the untested/stale groups and the widen. The filed problem has not rotted. Mechanism: the decision form allows one choice per decision, so a reader who cites the decision for one choice gets five, and a later change to one choice rewrites a file the others share. Corpus: concept:decision-artifact says a decision 'records a real architectural or technical choice: one shape adopted over identifiable alternatives'; that clause forces the split but not the grouping. Citers to repoint for a moved choice: decisions fixes-rerun-the-tests-they-reach, whole-file-ownership, live-sprints-brought-current-on-true-up, testing-runs-inside-the-sprint; code plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up, scripts/tests, scripts/plumbline; the decisions.md TOC regenerates. Harm: none an accept-list entry covers; this is a corpus-structure judgment. Options: A, three decisions grouped by the job each choice serves (the list with its stamps and support; the suite command with how runs are recorded and the second-round refusal; which stories a sprint plans, with the widen); cost: each group still bundles two or three choices with alternatives of their own, so a later sign-off review may find the same fault. B, one decision per listed choice, five in all; cost: more files and more citations to repoint, and choices that share a rationale restate it or cross-cite. A missed option: split by alternatives, so choices whose Alternatives entries are shared stay together and every other moves out; cost: the grouping turns on reading the Alternatives section, which the owner must check. Recommend B as the reading the decision-artifact clause gives most directly, with A where the owner judges each group to be one shape. Sibling: rule with test-speed-decision-bundles-several-choices; precedent: seed-recommended-never-required, already split out of tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome by the same sprint.

test-speed-decision-bundles-several-choices: Evidence, re-verified: .ok-planner/design/decisions/tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome.md (1207 words) still holds, beside its principle ('a test spends time only on proving its outcome'), the wait rule, and the named wastes: the three read points (write time, the build stages, after a failed whole-suite round), the failed-rewrite revert, the ranking by median seconds, the speed acceptance that a support-file change does not clear, the product-slow verdict, and no speed floor. The seed choice has moved to seed-recommended-never-required as filed; nothing else has. The filed problem has not rotted. Mechanism: the decision form allows one choice per decision, so a citation for one choice drags in the rest, and a change to one rewrites the shared file. Corpus: concept:decision-artifact, 'one shape adopted over identifiable alternatives', forces the split but not the grouping. Citers to repoint for a moved choice: decisions test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests, seed-recommended-never-required, team-execution-cold-gate; code plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up and scripts/tests; the decisions.md TOC regenerates. Harm: none an accept-list entry covers; corpus-structure judgment. Options: A, two decisions, the principle with its wastes and wait rule, and the speed read (ranking, acceptance, three read points, product-slow verdict, no speed floor) as one; cost: the speed read still bundles five choices with alternatives of their own, so a later review may find the same fault. B, one decision per listed choice; cost: six or so small decisions and more citations to repoint, and the read points, ranking, and acceptance share a rationale that each would restate or cross-cite. A missed option: three decisions, the principle with wastes and wait rule, the speed read's when (read points, revert) and its ranking with acceptance, and the product-slow verdict with no speed floor; cost: a grouping the owner must judge per choice. Recommend the same grouping rule the owner picks for the sibling. Sibling: rule with scenario-list-decision-bundles-several-choices.
